Agents often need paid APIs, data, or content mid-task, but access usually requires a person to sign up, add a payment method, and create an API key. items.title: Amazon Cognito now supports client ID metadata documents
items.content_snippet: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth client ID metadata documents (CIMD). Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. With CIMD, Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and AI agents can sign users in to your user pool without registering a separate app client. items.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput
items.content_snippet: With upgrades to its storage layer, Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput for many transactional workloads. Data loads finish sooner, and tables whose primary key always increases, such as tables keyed by a timestamp, an identity column, or a time-ordered ID like ULID or UUIDv7, see even greater benefits. items.content_snippet: AWS Lambda announces OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for Lambda durable functions. This helps you find bottlenecks in your system, root cause failures faster, and understand how your workflows behave in production. items.title: 3 ChatGPT Tips to Save Money
items.content_snippet: ChatGPT can help you find ways to save, whether you’re shopping for a desk chair or wondering what you’re still paying for after a free trial ends. Learn three ways to save money with ChatGPT. Use a product screenshot to compare prices before you buy, spot subscriptions you no longer use, and build a monthly budget that leaves room for things you enjoy. Looking for a better deal? Try ChatGPT before your next purchase: https://chatgpt.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign

items.title: Create and Share a Dashboard in ChatGPT
items.content_snippet: Turn your analysis into a dashboard your team can use. items.title: The Sweet Side of the Bitter Lesson — Thariq Shihipar, Independent
items.content_snippet: Vibe coding a fighting game left Thariq Shihipar unsure how his own characters worked. At CODE Summit 2026, he revisits the Bitter Lesson, Bash, React and MCP, contrasting AI’s jagged frontier with its smooth interior. His live demo uses readable specifications, custom scripting languages and IDE workflows to show how coding agents can preserve creative control and help bring about a software renaissance.
